welcome:
Welcome to golings — a rustlings-style tour of Go.
Run `golings watch` and start fixing exercises in order.
Each exercise has `// I AM NOT DONE` at the top — remove it once it compiles/passes.

exercises.name: intro1
exercises.hint: The program won't compile until you fix the obvious syntax error. Look at the Println call.

exercises.name: variables1
exercises.hint: You need to declare x. Use `var x int = 5` or `x := 5`.

exercises.name: variables2
exercises.hint: The `:=` shorthand only works inside functions. At package level use `var`.

exercises.name: variables3
exercises.hint: Constants are declared with `const`. They cannot be reassigned.

exercises.name: functions1
exercises.hint: A Go function: `func name(params) returnType { ... }`. The return type goes after the parameter list.

exercises.name: functions2
exercises.hint: Go supports multiple return values: `func divmod(a, b int) (int, int)`. Return both quotient and remainder.

exercises.name: if1
exercises.hint: No parentheses around the condition. `if x > 0 { ... } else { ... }`.

exercises.name: primitives1
exercises.hint: Go does not auto-convert numeric types. Use explicit conversions like `float64(i)` or `int(f)`.

exercises.name: slices1
exercises.hint: Use `append` to grow a slice. `append(s, 4)` returns a new slice — you must reassign.

exercises.name: maps1
exercises.hint: Create a map with `make(map[string]int)`. Reading a missing key returns the zero value; use the comma-ok form to detect absence.

exercises.name: structs1
exercises.hint: Define a struct with `type Point struct { X, Y int }`, then construct with `Point{X: 1, Y: 2}`.

exercises.name: methods1
exercises.hint: Pointer receiver: `func (c *Counter) Inc() { c.n++ }`. Value receivers can't mutate the original.

exercises.name: interfaces1
exercises.hint: Go interfaces are implemented implicitly. Just give your type the method with the matching signature.

exercises.name: errors1
exercises.hint: Return `error` as the last value. Use `errors.New("msg")` or `fmt.Errorf("...: %w", err)` to construct.

exercises.name: pointers1
exercises.hint: `&x` takes the address; `*p` dereferences. To mutate through a pointer parameter use `*p = newValue`.

exercises.name: goroutines1
exercises.hint: Use `sync.WaitGroup`. `wg.Add(1)` before launching, `defer wg.Done()` inside, `wg.Wait()` after.

exercises.name: channels1
exercises.hint: `ch := make(chan int)`. Send with `ch <- v`, receive with `v := <-ch`. Close with `close(ch)` when done sending.

exercises.name: generics1
exercises.hint: Generic syntax: `func Map[T, U any](s []T, f func(T) U) []U`. Type parameters in square brackets after the name.
